stories.title: Protecting fundamental rights in digitalised justice systems: a shared commitment of judges and lawyers – CCBE
stories.ltme_summary: The CCBE has published highlights of its plenary session and roundtable with the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg. The theme is protecting fundamental rights in digitalised justice systems as a shared commitment of judges and lawyers. The extract is only a short summary line, so the substance of the discussion is not visible here.
stories.hook: CCBE links judges and lawyers on protecting rights as justice systems digitalise

stories.title: SEC Freezes Backward Hat Capital in Alleged $560 Million AI Trading Fraud
Biglaw Firm Moves Associates To The ‘Cravath Scale’ — If They Hit Their Hours
Elite Litigation Boutique Pays Bonuses Up To $187.5K
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law reports that Reid Collins & Tsai is paying associate bonuses of $150,000 to $187,500 in its fourth-quarter round, on top of base salaries from $225,000. The firm says it has paid bonuses in all four quarters for the first time. Its senior founding partner says nine-figure revenue is becoming the norm.
stories.hook: Reid Collins & Tsai pays associate bonuses up to $187,500 in its fourth round

stories.title: Legal Ethics Roundup: DOJ Shuns ABA Ethics Rules, New Opinion On Client Fraud, Katie Zacharia Bar Probe, SCOTUS Reform, Multijurisdictional Practice, Judicial Disclosures, AI Ethics Tracker & More
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law's Legal Ethics Roundup covers several items, including a memo from acting deputy attorney general Trent McCotter telling Justice Department staff to avoid citing ABA materials, a new ABA opinion on noisy withdrawal, and a State Bar of California investigation into Katie Zacharia. It also features a LexisNexis interview on legal AI.
stories.hook: DOJ tells staff to avoid citing ABA materials, per Justice Department memo

stories.title: EU Charges Temu Over Illegal Product Sales
Morning Docket: 11.23.26
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law's morning docket lists several items, including DOJ orders for prosecutors to stop citing ABA resources, a Fifth Circuit ruling on COVID-era laws, and a rise in pro se filings linked to AI. Each item is a short link summary with a source. It is a roundup rather than a single development.
stories.hook: Morning Docket covers DOJ's ABA citation order and a rise in AI-linked pro se filings

stories.title: Is Going AI Native Incompatible with Big Law?
stories.ltme_summary: Artificial Lawyer asks whether going AI native is compatible with Big Law's business model. It cites Weil's planned Kepler spinout, Freshfields' reported plan to spin out its Lab group, and AI units at Kirkland, Goodwin, Wilson Sonsini and Cooley. The piece argues that human-hour billing sits uneasily with AI-native workflows that reduce human input.
stories.hook: Artificial Lawyer asks whether AI-native workflows can sit inside Big Law's time-based model

stories.title: Right About the Law, Wrong for the Company
stories.ltme_summary: Robb Hern, general manager of corporate legal at LexisNexis, argues that in-house lawyers must weigh company priorities, not only legal analysis, when answering business requests. He uses a hypothetical about training an AI assistant on customer support transcripts, setting out contract commitments, public promises and renewal timing, and options such as grounding without training.
stories.hook: LexisNexis's Robb Hern says in-house advice must reflect company commitments, not just the law

stories.title: Baker McKenzie’s AI Chief Explains Why The Law Business Model Is Changing
stories.ltme_summary: Lawyers Weekly interviewed Baker McKenzie's global chief innovation officer, Ben Allgrove, who says AI is now a commercial issue affecting pricing, recruitment and the billable hour. He expects consolidation among legal AI providers and says complex matters can need three or four tools. He also raises concern about training junior lawyers as routine work is automated.
stories.hook: Baker McKenzie's Ben Allgrove says legal AI vendors face consolidation and firms must rethink pricing

stories.title: Why Sidley is betting big on Weil teams as battle for clients heats up
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Business reports that Sidley Austin is hiring Weil teams after the collapse of Weil, with more than 200 Weil partners having found new homes. The article names Sidley's management committee chair Yvette Ostolaza, who previously spent 21 years at Weil, and lists other recent moves by rival firms.
stories.hook: More than 200 Weil partners have moved firms, with Sidley Austin recruiting heavily from the collapsed firm

stories.title: Winston Taylor makes up two London partners in first promotions as merged firm
stories.hook: Winston Taylor makes 23 partners in first post-merger round, two of them in London

stories.title: Ropes & Gray hires nine-partner team from Weil as Freshfields adds litigation duo in US
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Business reports that Ropes & Gray has hired more than 20 lawyers from Weil across the US and London, including nine partners, covering private equity, M&A, litigation and finance. The move follows Weil's announced plan to dissolve. The extract also lists related headlines about Freshfields and other laterals.
stories.hook: Ropes & Gray hires nine Weil partners as the Weil break-up draws in rival firms

stories.title: Heavyweight Quinn Emanuel partner in talks to buy Chelsea FC stake
In-house moves: Nestlé, RTL, Guardian Media appoint new legal chiefs
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Business reports that Nestlé has named Manuela Bernasconi as its group general counsel, with a seat on the group executive board. Bernasconi joined Nestlé in 2007 and became GC Zone Americas in January 2025. The article also lists other in-house legal appointments.
stories.hook: Nestlé appoints company veteran Manuela Bernasconi as group general counsel

stories.title: Convicted murderer passes SQE while on day release
European Court of Human Rights bans lawyer over fake cases in AI-drafted submissions
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Cheek reports that the European Court of Human Rights has barred a Romanian lawyer from representing litigants before it for two years. The court found numerous errors in her submissions, including non-existent cases and fictitious paragraphs, after she acknowledged using AI to draft them. The president approved the recommended ban earlier this month.
stories.hook: European Court of Human Rights bars Romanian lawyer for two years over AI-drafted fake citations

stories.title: AI risks de-skilling the next generation of lawyers, warns Supreme Court justice
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Cheek reports Lord Sales warning at a DAC Beachcroft conference that AI could erode junior lawyers' skills in research and document review. He suggested some training may need to happen without AI and that firms may need to train a smaller group more heavily. The article also cites comments by Lord Reed, Sir Geoffrey Vos and Sir Colin Birss on AI in courts.
stories.hook: Lord Sales warns AI could leave the next generation of lawyers without core skills

stories.title: Monday morning round-up
AI risk for remote legal teams
stories.ltme_summary: Nexa Law writes for Legal Futures on AI risk for remote legal teams after a lawyer was struck off for citing non-existent AI-generated cases in SRA v Kumar. It sets out the SRA warning notice of 17 August 2026 on AI misuse, and the Upper Tribunal's view on uploading confidential documents to public AI tools. It advises consultants to build in their own checks.
stories.hook: Nexa Law says remote lawyers carry sole responsibility for checking AI output under SRA rules

stories.title: Responsible business isn’t just a badge – it’s how you do business
stories.ltme_summary: DocumentDirect, a sponsor, writes about putting responsible business into practice at law firms. It describes the LawNet Excellence in Responsible Business Award, presented to Gardner Leader LLP, and discusses workload, wellbeing and supplier choice. The piece is sponsored content from a B Corp transcription and document production provider.
stories.hook: DocumentDirect says responsible business must reach supplier choices and workloads in law firms

stories.title: Brabners sharpens its international focus with new Head of Immigration
stories.hook: Brabners hires DLA Piper's UK immigration lead Hamza Malik as head of immigration

stories.title: Is AI set to reshape the traditional law firm rainmaker model?
stories.ltme_summary: LexisNexis research with more than 500 private practice lawyers in the UK and Ireland suggests the traditional rainmaker model is shifting towards value spread across the firm. The article says 20 per cent of firms rely completely or heavily on a handful of individuals for revenue. It links the shift to AI-enabled knowledge systems, citing that 65 per cent of lawyers use AI for legal research. The piece is sponsored content from LexisNexis.
stories.hook: LexisNexis research says AI is turning firm knowledge into an asset and weakening the rainmaker model

stories.title: Managing mental health risk in law firms: a shared responsibility
stories.ltme_summary: Lockton's Lucie Gosling-Myers writes for Legal Practice Management on how HR and risk teams in law firms can work together on mental health. She sets out operational, legal, reputational and financial risks, and cites LawCare's Life in the Law 2025 recommendations on workloads, management and flexible working.
stories.hook: Lockton says HR and risk teams should jointly manage mental health risk in law firms

stories.title: Assessing and managing your liabilities in a period of high claims inflation
Report: Wide AI adoption linked to significant revenue gains for UK and Irish law firms
stories.hook: Clio says wide AI adoption doubles the chance of significant revenue gains at UK and Irish firms

Ropes & Gray adds London finance partner James Crooks as nine join from Weil
Boutique Pallas beats Cravath scale with £190k associate bonuses
stories.ltme_summary: Nonbillable reports that litigation boutique Pallas Partners is offering London associates and counsel bonuses of up to £190,000, equal to $247,000, up $15,000 on last year. The structure includes extra payments at set billable-hour thresholds up to 2,500 hours. Pallas was founded in 2022 by Natasha Harrison.
stories.hook: Pallas Partners offers London associates bonuses up to £190,000, ahead of the Cravath scale

stories.title: How Proskauer got ahead of the private credit boom in London
Why AI startups should build governance early
stories.ltme_summary: Sifted argues that fast-growing European AI start-ups such as Lovable and ElevenLabs need governance earlier than past venture-backed firms did. It cites Lovable's security incident, bank contract demands under EU digital resilience rules, and the EU AI Act duties from December 2027. The piece is commentary on founder governance.
stories.hook: Sifted says European AI start-ups must build governance early as bank customers push contract terms

stories.title: Solicitor who made false email to keep client at bay struck off
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that solicitor Kimberley Clift has been struck off after sending a client a fabricated email and making false claims about chasing an SDLT refund. She admitted dishonesty and agreed the outcome with the SRA. The tribunal ordered her to pay £4,000 in costs.
stories.hook: Solicitor Kimberley Clift struck off after faking an email to a client about an SDLT refund

stories.title: In depth: Closing the social mobility gap
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette's in-depth piece says family connections and networks still give some young people an advantage in entering the legal profession. It cites Alan Milburn's NEET report, Flex Legal's trainee scheme, Freshfields' Molly Lewis and PRIMED for Law's Why Not Law programme, and Bexley Beaumont's Sutton Trust placements.
stories.hook: Law Society Gazette finds family networks still favour some young people entering the legal profession

stories.title: Burnham closes door on fully devolved Welsh justice
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that the UK government has, in a letter from prime minister Andy Burnham to the Welsh first minister, effectively ruled out a fully devolved Welsh justice system for now. The first minister Rhun ap Iorwerth criticised the reply. Browne Jacobson's Laura Hughes says the door to further devolution is not firmly closed.
stories.hook: Burnham letter rules out a fully devolved Welsh justice system for now, angering Cardiff

stories.title: Rajiv Menon KC: Contempt proceedings already having 'chilling effect'
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that Rajiv Menon KC says contempt proceedings have produced a chilling effect, with barristers toning down closing speeches. The proceedings concern his closing speech in a Palestine Action trial. His appeal is listed for the week beginning 14 December, to be heard by three judges.
stories.hook: Rajiv Menon KC says contempt proceedings are chilling criminal defence advocacy
entities: UCL Centre for Access to Justice

stories.title: Latest Anti-SLAPP bill sets 'almost impossibly high threshold'
stories.ltme_summary: The UK Anti-SLAPP Coalition says the latest private member's bill from John Whittingdale sets an almost impossibly high threshold for early dismissal of SLAPP claims. It sets out three conditions and a three-part strike-out test. The coalition will support the measure in principle, and the bill is due a second reading on Friday.
stories.hook: Anti-SLAPP Coalition warns Whittingdale bill sets an almost impossible early dismissal bar

stories.title: Single regulator should be on reform menu, consumer panel says
stories.ltme_summary: The Legal Services Consumer Panel welcomes the Commons justice committee's report on access to justice, which raises the possibility of a single legal services regulator. The panel urges a government commitment to a comprehensive review by 2029 and action within existing powers now. The government has yet to respond formally to the report.
stories.hook: Legal Services Consumer Panel backs a single regulator and calls for action before legislation

stories.title: SDT's £9,000 costs order set aside on appeal
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that a deputy High Court judge approved a consent order setting aside a Solicitors Disciplinary Tribunal costs order against Belinda Owusuah Sarkodie. The tribunal's dishonesty finding and her strike-off remain in effect. Pro bono counsel were praised for their work on the appeal.
stories.hook: High Court sets aside SDT costs order against struck-off solicitor Belinda Owusuah Sarkodie

stories.title: Federal Judge Rejects New Mexico Bar’s Broad Checks for Military Lawyers
stories.ltme_summary: The Lawyer Monthly reports that a US federal judge in New Mexico denied motions to dismiss a Justice Department suit over bar admission checks for military lawyers. The ruling of 19 November 2026 found both the state Supreme Court and the Board of Bar Examiners are licensing authorities under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act. The ruling does not decide whether violations occurred.
stories.hook: Federal judge rejects New Mexico bar's bid to escape DOJ suit over military lawyer licensing
entities: New Mexico Board of Bar Examiners

Alan Turing's legacy: 90 years of computing and the limits of AI
stories.ltme_summary: Solicitors Journal marks 90 years since Alan Turing's 1936 paper On Computable Numbers, outlining its role in the idea of the modern computer and the Hilbert Decision problem. The article links Turing's work to Colossus and argues that the paper shows limits to what computers can do, a point it draws out for technology lawyers facing AI questions.
stories.hook: Solicitors Journal marks 90 years since Turing's 1936 paper and links it to today's AI legal questions

stories.title: New digital solution for Guernsey trusts
Breaking Wall Street’s Partner Ceiling Way Back In 1944
Is Trump Ever To Blame? Should You Trust Him Or Our Enemies?
AI-native litigation firm goes live after SRA approval
stories.ltme_summary: Conclusive Legal, an AI-driven firm regulated by the SRA, has formally launched offering fixed-fee litigation and document review. Founder Jessica Fitzgerald says a solicitor checks all output and that the firm's proprietary document engine sits on top of a frontier AI model. Published prices start at £795 for a fast-track letter before action and £295 for a document review of up to 10 pages. Fitzgerald says the firm is looking for more consultant solicitors.
stories.hook: Conclusive Legal goes live as an SRA-regulated, AI-assisted litigation firm with published fixed fees from £795

stories.title: Sales: Train lawyers of future without AI so they can supervise it
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Futures reports that Lord Sales, deputy president of the Supreme Court, warned at a DAC Beachcroft conference that AI could deskill junior lawyers and judges. He suggested a smaller expert cadre of lawyers would need heavier investment, and that some training should be done without AI. He also floated AI as a first-instance decision-maker subject to human review.
stories.hook: Lord Sales warns AI deskilling could hollow out the training of junior lawyers and judges

stories.title: Project proves that digital property data can be shared safely
stories.ltme_summary: Legal Futures reports that a sandbox project led by the Council for Licensed Conveyancers showed digital property data can be shared securely. The project, funded by a £750,000 government grant from the Regulators' Pioneer Fund, involved 49 organisations over a year from October 2025. A report published on 23 November says it identified 15 pieces of legislation for government lawyers to review.
stories.hook: CLC-led property data sandbox shares data across 49 organisations and flags 15 laws for review
entities: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

stories.title: Transforming contract review at NetApp with Agiloft Astra
stories.ltme_summary: Agiloft publishes a customer story saying NetApp's legal team moved from manual redlining to Agiloft Astra, a contract AI platform with a Microsoft Word add-in. NetApp's Legal Operations Manager Shelle Elzer says the team ran an RFP and proof-of-concept tests before choosing Astra. The post is vendor-authored.
stories.hook: NetApp's legal team picks Agiloft Astra for AI contract review inside Microsoft Word, per Agiloft

stories.title: How to Improve Law Firm Productivity Without Losing Control
stories.ltme_summary: Neota Logic, a vendor of governed AI infrastructure for legal and compliance teams, publishes a guide on improving law firm and legal department productivity. It sets out a sequence: catalogue work, standardise intake and triage, and automate under audit trails and human checkpoints. The piece cites ACC and CLOC guidance and promotes Neota's own control layer over existing AI tools.
stories.hook: Neota Logic argues productivity gains need governance, audit trails and standardised intake before automation

stories.title: ESI Protocol Did Not Fully Describe a Metadata Privilege Log: eDiscovery Case Law
stories.hook: SDNY court holds an ESI protocol silent on narratives does not exclude descriptive entries in metadata privilege logs

stories.title: Legal Tech Companies Worldwide? There Are a Lot of Them: Legal Tech Trends
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin of eDiscovery Today, drawing on a Financial Times piece, says the legal tech market is crowded. He cites consultant Alex Baker's estimate of more than 5,000 legal tech companies worldwide and a Legaltech Hub count of 1,416 GenAI products from 1,117 vendors. Syllo, a sponsor of the blog, is named as having raised $30mn last year, and its CEO comments on marketing spend.
stories.hook: Commentator puts the number of legal tech companies worldwide above 5,000, citing an FT report

stories.title: Interview with Adam Rouse on The Evolution of Legal Data Intelligence and AI Adoption in Corporate Legal Departments
stories.ltme_summary: Doug Austin interviews Adam Rouse, Relativity's Director of Corporate Legal Community Engagement, about his move from in-house practice and the Legal Data Intelligence initiative. They discuss in-house departments insourcing work, AI adoption barriers in corporate legal, and Relativity's conversational AI for lawyers. The interview was recorded at RelFest Chicago.
stories.hook: Relativity's Adam Rouse says corporate legal AI adoption is held back by top-down mandates and cautious committees

stories.title: Australians could soon be able to sue social media giants for online harm
stories.ltme_summary: Australia's federal government has struck a deal with the Greens to pass Labor's Digital Duty of Care laws, which could let Australians sue social media companies such as Meta and TikTok over harm linked to platform design. RMIT senior lecturer Dr Tina Popa, quoted in the RMIT release, says the reform would add a private right to compensation to existing regulatory action.
stories.hook: Australia's Digital Duty of Care deal could give citizens a private right to sue Meta and TikTok

stories.title: Ten Years of Mindfulness Webinars Later, Half of Lawyers Are Still Burned Out
stories.ltme_summary: A US study published in the Journal of Affective Disorders in September, by Patrick Krill and Justin Anker with the ABA Commission on Lawyer Assistance Programs, reports that 47.4 per cent of more than 37,000 weighted respondents screened positive for high burnout. LawFuel says rates of depression, anxiety and stress have risen since the 2016 benchmark, and that lawyers working 71 or more hours a week are far more likely to report high stress.
stories.hook: ABA-backed US study finds 47.4 per cent of lawyers screen positive for high burnout
entities: ABA Commission on Lawyer Assistance Programs

stories.title: Smart Property Data Trust Framework pilot hailed as success
Lawtech incubator receives £3m MoJ funding to encourage AI adoption
stories.ltme_summary: Today's Conveyancer reports on a Council for Licensed Conveyancers project that the headline describes as a £3m Ministry of Justice grant to a lawtech incubator to encourage AI adoption. The extract covers only a strapline about a Smart Property Data Trust Framework pilot being hailed as a success, so the link between that pilot and the headline funding is unclear from the extract alone.
stories.hook: Lawtech incubator headline cites £3m MoJ funding for AI adoption; extract only shows a property data pilot

stories.title: Nationwide offers to help legal professionals with cyber-attack resilience
stories.ltme_summary: Today's Conveyancer reports that Nationwide is offering help to legal professionals on cyber-attack resilience. The extract is a repeated strapline about a Smart Property Data Trust Framework pilot and does not describe the offer. Details of the scheme, its scope and any cost would need to come from the full article.
stories.hook: Nationwide offers legal professionals cyber-attack resilience support, per Today's Conveyancer

stories.title: Commonhold reforms raise questions over the future of leasehold
SQE proposals could split exams to tackle ‘fatigue’ and increase resit options
stories.ltme_summary: Today's Wills and Probate reports proposals to split Solicitors Qualifying Examination sittings to reduce candidate fatigue and add resit options. The extract is a mismatched strapline about pet and children guardianship and does not describe the SQE proposals, so the proposing body and timetable cannot be confirmed from it.
stories.hook: SQE proposals would split exams to reduce fatigue and widen resit options, according to Today's Wills and Probate

stories.ltme_summary: Elevate has published a post about its ELM Playbook Word plugin, which covers suggested wording and redlining. The extract is only the outlet's summary line, so the feature detail comes from the headline alone.

stories.title: The full-portfolio view: how risk intelligence for consulting firms creates strategic advantage at scale
stories.ltme_summary: Intapp has published a piece on risk intelligence for consulting firms, arguing that portfolio-level views of conflicts and engagements help firms manage exposure. The article promotes its Intapp Celeste platform and related DealCloud tooling.

stories.title: Cocktail Party Coverage: What the War Exclusion Actually Requires, and Why Europe’s Freezers Still Don’t Get There
stories.ltme_summary: Integreon has published a commentary on the war exclusion in cyber insurance after November 2026 attacks on European supermarket refrigeration, which France attributed to Iran. The piece argues the exclusion is not triggered on these facts.

stories.title: Legal Doesn’t Have to Learn AI’s Lessons the Hard Way
stories.ltme_summary: Integreon's Chief Executive, writing after the TLTF Summit Legal Leaders Forum, argues legal can learn from earlier technology waves rather than repeat them. He cites figures that the average legal organisation uses 183 AI tools and that 85 per cent describe their AI environments as siloed. The post is a vendor thought-leadership piece.
stories.hook: Integreon says the average legal organisation uses 183 AI tools, with 85 per cent of environments siloed

stories.title: Your Legal Team Just Got Smaller. The Work Didn’t.
stories.ltme_summary: Integreon, an alternative legal service provider, argues in a vendor post that legal departments facing headcount cuts can use ALSPs to keep contract review, litigation document review and routine work moving. It says this avoids higher outside counsel spend and allows the in-house team to focus on higher-value work.
stories.hook: Integreon argues ALSPs can close the capacity gap left by in-house layoffs without rebuilding headcount

stories.title: Your Legal Department Doesn’t Need Another Transformation Plan. It Needs a Way to Execute.
stories.ltme_summary: Integreon, an alternative legal service provider, argues in a vendor post that corporate legal departments should use ALSPs to turn transformation plans into action. It names contract management, legal spend and document review as starting points and says ALSPs can help sustain change through managed services and reporting.
stories.hook: Integreon says ALSPs can turn legal department transformation plans into sustained change

stories.title: Mitratech Brings ARIES™ to OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Extending Legal Matters, Spend, and Tasks into Customers’ Everyday AI Workflows
stories.ltme_summary: Mitratech says it has connected its ARIES platform to OpenAI's ChatGPT through a new connector for TeamConnect customers. The connector lets users work with legal matters, spend and tasks in natural language within existing permissions. The extract is a summary line only.
stories.hook: Mitratech connects ARIES and TeamConnect data to ChatGPT through a new natural-language connector
